or_x_tasmanian_devil.blurb: Tasmanian Devil is a freestanding pinnacle in the Smith Rock area of Central Oregon, set away from the busiest walls and reached by a longer approach than the main canyon crags. It holds eleven sport routes on tuff, with a few easy lines in the 5.7 to 5.8 range, a lone 5.10, and a solid block of 5.11s and 5.12s. The south side is the main wall, with a reddish slab and some steep overhanging extensions above it. Boulders sit around the base, though hauling a pad up there is a chore in the wind. Expect quiet, committed days rather than a social scene. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons; summer sun can be punishing.

sd_pheromone_wall.blurb: Pheromone Wall is a sport crag within the Blue Sky area of Spearfish Canyon in the northern Black Hills. Thirteen bolted routes span a wide range: a couple of easy lines around 5.7 to 5.8, a pair of 5.9s, then a steep jump into the hard stuff, with a handful of 5.11s, three 5.12s and four 5.13s. The centrepiece is a big streaked buttress carrying the longest lines on the wall, with good views down the canyon. The approach is short, following the main Blue Sky trail left past the Iron Horse wall, then a faint path climbing the hillside to the base. Best suited to climbers comfortable on technical limestone vertical to mildly overhanging terrain.
